rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (365.78, the best so far): the oval finished 17 of 20 runs (finish time about 1.92 s, max_error 0.044 m), so the design works on gentle curves. The s-bend had max_error 0.0613 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and 19 of 20 runs left the track. The slalom progressed only 0.117 and left the track in all 20 runs. Line-loss events were 0.3 on the oval and 0.2 on the slalom, so the robot loses the line briefly on bends before it leaves. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 m at body_width 0.12 and cannot be raised by body width within the contract, so the error must be reduced. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.3 to 1.1. The oval finishes in about 1.9 s at 1.3, leaving room in the 3.0 s limit, and the s-bend max_error is just over the limit, so speed is the cheapest lever. (2) Sensor span widened from x = +/-0.06 to +/-0.08, the contract maximum, so the line stays under an outer sensor on sharper bends and line loss should fall. (3) Sensors moved forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07 to give more lookahead, which reduces the lag that causes overshoot on the s-bend and slalom. (4) kd 0.5 to 0.6 for extra damping on the alternating slalom corners; steering_oscillation is moderate at 0.26, so this is a small step. kp stays at 1.6 and line_loss stays at last_direction so that only the bend-handling changes vary. Expected result: fewer off-track ends on the s-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.05 m on the s-bend, and completion on the oval with a completion time under 2.5 s. Hypotheses: speed and lookahead are the main drivers of bend error, and line loss on the slalom comes from the narrow span. Measurements wanted next: max_error and progress per track, line_loss_events on the slalom, and completion_time on the oval to see how much time the speed reduction costs.
